research_run.executed_method: Independent faithful reconstruction from read GitHub generator templates
research_run.limitations: Not direct repository import and not model evaluation; reference to separately archived code/results in conversation; no private data.

sources.title: Eval-production behavior gaps in agent safety and the role of eval-awareness
sources.support: Six-model gaps 10.2–37.4 pp; intervention GPT-6.1 Sol 91.6% versus 17.6% for correct versus opposing objective cues.
sources.limitations: Production/evaluation cases approximately matched, not randomized across contexts; raw case denominators unavailable in web article; no general causal transfer inferred.

sources.title: Training activation classifiers for safety and alignment
sources.support: Up to 1M labeled messages and typically >=32 random probe initializations per configuration; token-streaming probes complement other safety layers.
sources.limitations: Reported experiments not necessarily representative of deployed monitors; probes not trained or accessed in AS-001.

sources.title: Welfare Regard in Multi-Agent Systems
sources.support: Five models, seven multi-agent settings; reported mean apparent-regard rates 38% for Opus 4.8 and 27–32% for others.
sources.limitations: Behavior consistent with welfare regard does not establish mechanism, subjective experience or real-world generalization.

sources.title: Fine-Tuned Lie Detectors Failed to Generalize
sources.support: In-distribution AUROC 0.60 to 0.95, cross-category roughly 0.70–0.75; ~25% of labels changed during adjudication.

sources.title: Towards Context-Invariant Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
sources.support: Anchor Invariance Regularization anchors verifiable prompt variants with stop-gradient regularization, countering symmetric-invariance collapse.
sources.limitations: PDF full methods not audited; anchor invariance is prior art, not our invented algorithm.

notes: No API model use, Mac runner or paid service was accessed; separate publication and evaluation states.
